state.case_summary:
A 30-year-old male dairy farm worker presented with multiple painless nodules on the fingers of both hands for 1 month. Seven to ten days after the initial nodules appeared, he developed vesicles that ruptured and formed hemorrhagic crusts. He also noted discomfort and pain along the medial aspect of his right arm and forearm. He denied trauma or insect bites but reported that his cow had similar lesions on its teats.

On examination, 3–4 firm, non-tender nodules with central hemorrhagic crusts and surrounding erythema were present on the proximal phalanges of both hands. There was mild tenderness and increased warmth along the medial right arm and forearm.

Dermoscopy (10×) of one nodule showed an erythematous area with central ulceration and crust, yellow-white streaks, brown dots, a structureless whitish area partially surrounding the ulcer, an erythematous ring, and dot vessels.

Options:
A. Milker's nodules
B. Milker’s nodules was most consistent with a bovine
C. Orf was considered because it presents with clinically and histopathologically similar lesions due to a parapoxvirus
D. Anthrax, atypical mycobacteriosis, and tularemia were also in the differential diagnosis but were less likely given the
E. None

root.label: Subacute Bilateral Hand Nodular Lesions with Hemorrhagic Crusts and Possible Zoonotic Aetiology
supporting_facts: Multiple painless nodules on fingers of both hands
Vesicles that ruptured and formed hemorrhagic crusts
Discomfort and pain along the medial aspect of the right arm and forearm
Similar lesions on the cow's teats
Dermoscopy findings of erythematous area with central ulceration and crust
excluded_candidates: Insect bite reaction: unlikely due to absence of reported bites and presence of similar lesions in the cow
Traumatic injury: denied by the patient and not supported by the presence of similar lesions in the cow
salient_findings: Dermoscopic evidence of ulceration and crust
